name: Translate Your Website – WeLocale AI Multilingual Translation
author: sserghei

sections.description:
Visitors who read your site in their own language stay longer, understand more and are more likely to get in touch or buy. WeLocale is an automatic website translation plugin for WordPress. It translates your WordPress website into 50+ languages with AI-powered translation, adds a multilingual language switcher, and on the Pro and Scale plans outputs hreflang tags for multilingual SEO. Connect once, press one button, and your site can reach a new audience in minutes: no developer, no code changes, no copying keys between tabs.

You run everything inside WordPress, in one control panel under Settings -> WeLocale. The same site can also be managed in your WeLocale dashboard at welocale.net.

How it works

  1. Connect in one step. Press “Create a free account” (or “Sign in and connect”). WeLocale opens in a new tab, adds your site to your account and sends you back. The WordPress screen updates by itself. There is no key to copy.
  2. Pick your languages. Say which language your site is written in and choose what to translate into. A counter shows how many languages your plan allows.
  3. Let WeLocale find your text. A small script reads the text on your pages as they are opened, and on paid plans a whole-site scan finds all of it in one go.
  4. Translate with AI, then edit. The AI translates each text once and the result is saved, so the next visitor gets it instantly. You can change any translation, and your edits are never overwritten by AI.
  5. Go live when you are ready. Test the translated site yourself in preview mode, then publish it for visitors.

Translations are stored in your WeLocale account, not in your WordPress database. Your posts, pages and theme stay exactly as they are, so it works with any theme and page builder.

The control panel in your WordPress admin

  • Overview – is your site live, how much of your plan you have used (AI words, words on your site, languages), how far each language is translated, how many pages and texts were found, and when your pages were last scanned.
  • Languages – set your original language and pick the languages to translate into, with a live count against your plan.
  • Switcher – choose the style of the language switcher (floating light or dark, pills, flags, an icon, or a bar across the page) with a live preview. A bar can sit at the top or the bottom of the page. Choose which languages visitors can pick. On the Pro and Scale plans you can also match each visitor’s language automatically or show everyone one fixed language.
  • Content – three parts. Texts: read, search, filter and edit every translation in place; coloured dots show what the AI generated, what a person edited and what still needs translation, each edit keeps a version, and a Previous button takes you back. Pages: the pages WeLocale has found and when each was last read. Translate with AI: translate everything that is missing for one language or all of them, follow the progress and cancel a run whenever you want. If AI translation is not available (limit reached, subscription ended, not in your plan), the button stays visible and says why.
  • Finding your text – string discovery collects new text from your pages as visitors open them and works on every plan. The whole-site scan, available on paid plans, visits every page for you.
  • Preview mode – see the translated site yourself, logged in as an administrator, while visitors still see the original, then publish with one click.
  • Settings – switch the whole site, the switcher and translations, and string discovery on or off; leave page builders and the Customizer alone; set scan rules (CSS selectors to include or exclude); list the domains allowed to show translations; disconnect.
  • Your plan – what your plan includes. Features that are not in your plan are marked with a lock and the plan that unlocks them, with a link to your WeLocale dashboard.
  • Help – how each part works, answers to common questions and a way to reach support with your setup details attached.

Which plan is for what

  • Free – a permanent plan, no credit card needed, to try WeLocale on one website with two languages and a limited number of words.
  • Starter – more websites, languages and words, whole-site scanning and more switcher styles, including a bar.
  • Pro – everything in Starter plus automatic visitor language, a fixed language for everyone, hreflang and SEO tags for translated pages, all switcher styles and removing the WeLocale credit from the switcher.
  • Scale – the same features as Pro with the highest limits.

Plans, limits and prices: https://welocale.net/pricing

Why WeLocale?

  • Reach people in their own language – translate once and every visitor sees your site in the language they pick, or the one their browser uses on Pro and Scale.
  • AI-powered, human-editable – translations are generated automatically and you can change any of them.
  • No code changes – your theme and your content stay as they are. Translation happens in the visitor’s browser.
  • 50+ languages, including Spanish, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, Dutch, Polish, Japanese, Chinese, Arabic and Russian.
  • A translated text is counted once – it is stored in your account and is not charged again when visitors load it.

WooCommerce

WeLocale translates the visible text of your WooCommerce pages: product names and descriptions, categories, cart, checkout and order confirmation. Emails your store sends and text inside third-party payment forms that load in an iframe are not translated, because WeLocale translates pages in the visitor’s browser.

Page builders and themes

WeLocale translates the rendered output of a page, so it does not depend on how the page was built: block editor, classic editor, Elementor, Divi, Beaver Builder and custom themes. By default the script is switched off inside the Elementor, Divi, Beaver Builder, Oxygen, Brizy and WPBakery editors and in the Customizer preview so it does not get in your way. You can change this in Settings.

What gets translated

  • Pages, posts and custom post types, as the visitor sees them
  • WooCommerce product pages, cart and checkout
  • Navigation menus, widgets, sidebars and theme text visible on the front end

Search engines may still see your original language, because translation happens in the browser. Pro and Scale add hreflang tags; see the FAQ for details.

External service

This plugin connects your site to WeLocale (https://welocale.net), a third-party website-translation service, and requires a WeLocale account (free to create, no credit card).
Terms of Service: https://welocale.net/terms. Privacy Policy: https://welocale.net/privacy.

1. On your public pages, when the widget loads. The plugin adds the WeLocale script (https://welocale.net/widget/latest/loader.js) to your front-end pages with your site’s public app key. The script then sends to welocale.net: the public app key, the path of the page, the visitor’s browser language and time zone (to get your settings and translations), and, while page scanning is on, the visible text found on the page, the full page address, the browser user agent, language and time zone (so new text can be translated). The script stores the visitor’s chosen language and downloaded translations in the browser’s localStorage. It sets no cookies. It does not run in wp-admin.

2. In wp-admin, only when an administrator uses the panel. When you press “Create a free account” or “Sign in and connect”, your browser opens https://welocale.net/connect in a new tab with your site address, the address of your Settings -> WeLocale page and a one-time check value; after you confirm, your browser returns to your site with the public app key and a one-time code. Your server then sends the one-time code to https://welocale.net/api/v1/account/token_exchange and receives a private access token, which is stored in your WordPress database (option welocale_api_token) and is never printed in a page. From then on, only while an administrator has the WeLocale panel open or presses a button there, your server sends requests to https://welocale.net/api/v1/account with that token: it reads your website’s status, plan usage, languages, pages and translations, and it sends what you change: languages, widget and switcher settings, scan rules, edited translations, and requests to start an AI translation or a scan. The panel shows the email address of the WeLocale account the site is connected to. None of these requests is made from your public pages. The token can read and edit this one website’s translations, languages and settings and start AI runs and scans, and it cannot sign in to or change anything else in your account.

Disconnecting (Settings tab) revokes the token at WeLocale and deletes the token and the app key from your site. Deleting the plugin removes the plugin settings and the token from your site.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate the plugin (Plugins -> Add New, search “WeLocale”, or upload the zip).
  2. Go to Settings -> WeLocale and press “Create a free account” (or “Sign in and connect” if you already have one). WeLocale opens in a new tab.
  3. In the new tab, sign up or sign in, and confirm your site. Your site is added to your account for you. You can close that tab: the WeLocale screen in WordPress updates by itself.
  4. Pick your original language and the languages to translate into, press Continue, then “Translate with AI” and “Show the switcher”.
  5. Open your site in another tab to see it. Manage languages, the switcher, translations and settings from Settings -> WeLocale. Changing your plan happens in your WeLocale dashboard.
sections.faq:
Is the plugin free, and do I need an account?

The plugin is free. It connects your site to WeLocale, which needs an account, and the account is free to create: Free plan, no card required, and it never expires. A paid plan is only needed when you outgrow the Free plan. Plans and limits: https://welocale.net/pricing

Which plan do I need?

Free is for trying it on one website. Starter adds more languages and words, whole-site scanning and more switcher styles. Pro adds automatic visitor language, hreflang and SEO tags for translated pages and removing the WeLocale credit. Current limits are always on https://welocale.net/pricing

How do I connect my site?

Go to Settings -> WeLocale and press “Create a free account” (or “Sign in and connect”). WeLocale opens in a new tab, adds your site to your account and sends you back. There is no key to copy.

Which languages can I translate into?

50+ languages, including Spanish, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, Dutch, Polish, Japanese, Chinese, Arabic and Russian. Your plan sets how many you can use at once.

What do my visitors see, and how does the language switcher work?

Visitors see your site in your original language until they pick another one in the language switcher. The switcher is a small control on your page (floating, pills, flags, an icon or a bar, depending on your plan), and the chosen language is remembered in the visitor’s browser. On Pro and Scale you can also match each visitor’s browser language automatically or show everyone one fixed language.

Can I check the translations before visitors see them?

Yes. Turn on Preview mode in Settings. Only you, logged in as an administrator, see the translated site. Turn it off to publish.

Can I edit the translations?

Yes, any of them. Open Settings -> WeLocale -> Content to read, search and edit every text in place. A text you edit is never overwritten by AI, and each edit keeps a version you can go back to.

Will it slow down my site?

The script is added in the footer and loads after your page has started rendering, so it does not block rendering. Translations are cached in the visitor’s browser after the first load. Visitors reading your original language download the script but have nothing replaced.

Is it good for SEO? Does it translate URLs?

Translation happens in the visitor’s browser, so every language uses the same URL and slugs stay in the original language. Search engines that do not run JavaScript see your original text, and we cannot promise that search engines will index or rank a translation. On Pro and Scale, WeLocale adds hreflang tags and translates the page title and meta description for translated languages, also in the browser and not in your HTML source. If translated URLs that search engines index separately are essential for you today, a plugin that creates them is a better fit.

Does it work with Elementor, Divi and the block editor?

WeLocale translates the rendered page, so it does not need to know how the page was built, and it works with block editor, classic editor, Elementor, Divi, Beaver Builder and custom themes. The script is switched off inside the Elementor, Divi, Beaver Builder, Oxygen, Brizy and WPBakery editors and in the Customizer preview so it does not get in your way.

Does it work with WooCommerce?

WeLocale translates the rendered page, so WooCommerce product, cart and checkout pages are translated like any other page. It does not translate emails or text inside payment forms loaded in an iframe.

What happens if I deactivate the plugin or my subscription ends?

If you deactivate the plugin, the script stops loading and visitors see your original site. If a paid subscription ends, translation pauses and visitors see your original site too; your translations and settings stay in your WeLocale account and resume when you renew. The Free plan has no end date.

What happens when I reach my plan limit?

Texts that are already translated keep working. New text stays in the original language until you upgrade. The panel shows a notice when a limit is reached.

Do I have to keep the WeLocale panel open?

No. Translations are served to visitors from WeLocale whether or not you are logged in to WordPress.

Where are my translations stored, and what data goes to WeLocale?

Translations are stored in your WeLocale account, not in your WordPress database. The script on your public pages sends the public app key, the page path and the visitor’s browser language and time zone, and while page scanning is on, the visible text found on the page, the page address and the browser user agent. The script sets no cookies and keeps the visitor’s chosen language in the browser’s localStorage. The full list is under “External service” above.

Browsers can translate pages too. How is WeLocale different?

Browsers can translate pages too, and it is usually free. WeLocale lets you choose the languages, edit the wording and place the language switcher on your page.

How is it different from Weglot or WPML?

All three translate a WordPress site, but in different ways. WeLocale translates in the visitor’s browser with one script, no copies of your posts and no translated URLs. Tools that create a separate indexable URL per language, or a separate post per language, give you more control over search results and slugs and are the better choice if you need translated URLs. Our comparison pages say where each tool is stronger: https://welocale.net/weglot-alternative and https://welocale.net/wpml-alternative

How do I get support?

Start with the support chat on welocale.net, or write to us through https://welocale.net/contact. The Help tab in the plugin has a box of setup details to paste in, with no passwords or keys. Response times depend on your plan, and the Free plan has community support. Support questions about the plugin are also answered in the support forum here.

Which languages is the plugin panel itself available in?

The control panel is translated into Spanish, Brazilian Portuguese, German, French, Italian and Polish. WordPress shows it in the language set for your admin (Settings -> General -> Site Language, or your profile language); in other languages it is shown in English.

How do I disconnect, and how do I delete my data?

Settings tab -> Disconnect. This revokes the access token at WeLocale, removes the token and the app key from your site, and the script stops loading. Your translations stay in your WeLocale account until you delete the account in your dashboard (Profile -> Delete account), which removes your websites and translations. Deleting the plugin from the Plugins screen also removes its settings and the token from your site.

How do I exclude content from translation?

Add the HTML attribute translate="no" or the class notranslate to any element, or exclude parts of every page with the exclude selectors under Settings -> WeLocale -> Settings -> Scan rules.
sections.changelog:
1.3.1

  • The control panel is now translated into Brazilian Portuguese, German, French, Italian and Polish. WordPress shows it in the language set for your admin (Settings -> General -> Site Language, or your profile language).

1.3.0

  • A control panel inside WordPress. Overview, Languages, Switcher, Content, Settings and Help tabs let you manage your translations without leaving your site: choose languages, pick and place the language switcher, edit any translated text, translate with AI, scan your whole site and see your plan and limits.
  • Connect in one step. A new Connect button opens WeLocale in a new tab; the plugin updates by itself when you come back. Your App Key is no longer copied by hand.
  • Preview mode. Test the translated site as an administrator before visitors see it, then publish with one click.
  • Every feature is visible on every plan. What is not in your plan is marked with a lock and the plan that includes it, and links to your WeLocale dashboard to upgrade.
  • AI translation can be cancelled while it runs, and its buttons say why they are blocked (limit reached, subscription ended, not in your plan).
  • The widget does not load inside Elementor, Divi, Beaver Builder and Customizer previews (can be turned off in Settings).
  • Safer connection: the plugin talks to WeLocale with a token limited to your own website, which is revoked when you disconnect or uninstall.
  • Control panel strings translated for Spanish. Other languages of the new screens follow in a later update.

1.2.6

  • Re-release to fix a version mismatch flagged by WordPress.org: the 1.2.5 SVN tag was cut before trunk’s Version header was updated to match, so the published tag’s plugin file still read 1.2.4 even though the readme and download link said 1.2.5. No functional change from 1.2.5.

1.2.5

  • The plugin’s own screens are now translated: the bundled language files are loaded.

1.2.4

  • One-click connect. The settings screen has a Connect button that opens WeLocale, creates the website for you and brings the App Key back automatically.
  • A permanent free plan: one website, two languages and 5,000 source words, with no credit card and no expiry date.

1.2.3

  • Corrected the plugin’s own settings screen and FAQ, and linked the readme to the plans page.

1.2.2

  • Corrected a claim in the description about word allowances.

1.2.1

  • Compatibility with WordPress 7.1.
  • Clearer plugin title and description so the plugin is easier to find when searching for “translate”.

1.2.0

  • Expanded documentation: WooCommerce section, page builder compatibility list, new FAQ entries.
  • All screenshots standardized to consistent resolution.

1.1.0

  • Language switcher now defaults to bottom-right corner on initial load.
  • Improved plugin listing with screenshots and expanded documentation.

1.0.0

  • Initial release: connect a WordPress site to WeLocale via App Key and load the AI translation widget.
